Thousands of cyclists will take part in either the 50km or the 10km ride for Spring Cycle from North Sydney to Olympic Park via Pyrmont. Road closures will be in place along the first 10km to Pyrmont, from there cyclists will continue on to Olympic Park sharing roads with motorists and abiding by general road rules.

ROAD CLOSURES - 4AM TO 11:30AM:

  • Cahill Expressway and Sydney Harbour Bridge: from 4am to 10:30am the Cahill Expressway lanes 7 and 8, including Mount St and High St on ramps will be closed. On the Sydney Harbour Bridge deck, lanes 3 and 6 will be closed – two lanes will remain open in both directions under a reduced 40km/h speed limit. From 4am to 11am the Cahill Expressway Circular Quay Overpass will be closed in both directions.
  • North Sydney between 4am and 11am: Miller St from Falcon St to Pacific Hwy, Berry St from Pacific Hwy to Walker St, sections of Arthur St, Carlow St, Blue St and surrounding local roads including the High St bridge on-ramp.
  • Sydney CBD, The Rocks and Millers Point between 4am and 11am: including Hickson Rd / Sussex St from Towns Place to King St and sections of Argyle St, Dalgety Rd and Upper Fort St.
  • Western Distributor from Pyrmont to the City from 4am to 11.15am: including Pyrmont on-ramp, Fig St on-ramp and King St off-ramp. Citybound motorists from the Anzac Bridge will be diverted via the Bathurst St off-ramp to re-join the Harbour Bridge or access City North via Harbour St or Kent St.
  • Pyrmont and Ultimo between 4am and 11:30am: on sections of Pyrmont St, Pirrama Rd, Pyrmont Bridge Rd, Union St, Murray St and surrounding local roads. Cycleway closure from 4am to 11am on Union St between Edward St and Murray St (eastbound)
  • Sydney Olympic Park between 7:30am and 3pm: Some closures will be in place on sections of Hill Rd, Edwin Flack Ave and Olympic Blvd.

Special event clearways will be in place on roads along sections of the course in North Sydney, Millers Point and Pyrmont between 3am and 11am and in Five Dock/Concord between 5am and 11am.

With around 80,000 people expected to attend the NRL & NRLW Grand Final, significant delays are expected on roads approaching the precinct.  

Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads approaching Olympic Park including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

  • PARKING: Do not drive unless you have pre-booked parking. Pre-book online ahead of time to secure a space as parking will be in high demand. A flat rate $35 parking fee applies. 
  • If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.
  • Carpool with your group and allow plenty of extra travel time as traffic will be heavy during the busy weeknight peak.
  • Alternatively, consider parking at a nearby train station commuter car park and continuing your trip by train to Olympic Park, at no extra cost.

Roads will be closed in the Sydney Olympic Park precinct between 1.30am Sat 4 Oct and 1am Tue 7 Oct, including sections of Olympic Blvd, Dawn Fraser Ave, Edwin Flack Ave and surrounding roads. Heavy traffic is expected, follow directions of traffic controllers and NSW Police.

For road closure details and locations, see visit the Sydney Olympic Park Authority interactive map.

The Sculpture by the Sea exhibition returns to the Bondi to Tamarama coastal walk for 18 days from Friday 17 October to Monday 3 November.

With around 450,000 people expected to visit throughout the exhibition, significant delays are expected on roads approaching Bondi and Tamarama beaches including Bondi Rd, Old South Head Rd and Syd Einfeld Dr. 

Changed traffic conditions and parking restrictions will be in place.

Motorists should avoid driving through the area where possible or expect delays and allow plenty of extra travel time, particularly on weekends.

Road closures and changed traffic conditions:

  • Local roads in Bondi, Bronte and Tamarama will be closed at various times during the event including sections of Notts Ave, Fletcher St, Marks Ln, Kenneth St, Bayview St, Wolaroi Cr, Ashley St, Turner St, Cross St, Birrell St, Darling St, Silva St, Illawong Ave, Carlisle St, Rowland Ave and Wilga St. Access for residents will be maintained.
  • One-way traffic conditions will be in place on roads around the coastal walk between 7.30am Friday 17 October and 6.30am Tuesday 4 November. Allow extra travel time, follow the directions of traffic controllers and exercise caution.

Special event clearways: Strict parking restrictions will be in effect each weekend of the event on Saturday 18 and Sunday 19 October, Saturday 25 and Sunday 26 October and Saturday 1 and Sunday 2 November at the following times and locations:

  • 7am to 2pm: Bondi Rd between Old South Head and opposite Sandridge St at Bondi Beach (northern side)
  • 12pm midday to 7pm: Bondi Rd between Sandridge St at Bondi Beach and Oxford St at Bondi Junction (southern side)
  • 8am to 4pm: Campbell Pde between Queen Elizabeth Drive and Beach Rd at Bondi Beach (Eastern side)

Special event clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types, and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed it will be relocated to the nearest legal parking space, use the Find My Car website or call 132 701 to find its new location.

Kevin Hart at Qudos Bank Arena on Friday from 8pm.

Traffic may be heavier than usual on roads approaching Sydney Olympic Park as attendees travel to the event during the busy evening peak.

Motorists should allow extra travel time on the M4, Parramatta Road, Homebush Bay Drive and Concord Road. 

If you have to drive, carpool with your group pre-book your parking online ahead of time to secure a space – available until 11:59pm the night before the event unless sold out prior. 

To get to your carpark and avoid the heavy traffic congestion expected at the Homebush Bay Drive roundabout, use Silverwater Road, Holker Street and Hill Road

Roads may be closed in the precinct, for closure details, visit the Sydney Olympic Park interactive map for more details.

RAAF Richmond Airshow on Saturday and Sunday. Gates will open at 9am, with flying displays to be conducted from 11am to 4pm each day.

With up to 40,000 attendees expected each day over the weekend, heavy traffic is expected in Clarendon and surrounding suburbs approaching the airbase.

Motorists should allow extra travel time on roads including Hawkesbury Valley Way, Blacktown Rd, The Northern Rd and Richmond Rd.

Limited paid-parking will be available at Hawkesbury Showground (pre-purchased ticket required), with access via Blacktown Road only. There is no access to the carpark from Hawkesbury Valley Way. Attendees are encouraged to arrive early to avoid delays and allow time for parking and shuttle transfers.

The RAAF runway will be closed from 11:00 am. During this time, attendees will need to wait for shuttle services from the ticket check-in area to the entertainment zone.


Road closures

  • Racecourse Rd will be closed at Hawkesbury Valley Way and the Rail line crossing from 6am to 6pm on Saturday and Sunday for the safety of crowds getting to and from the event via the train station.
  • Sections of Hobart St, Dight St and Percival St surrounding the airbase will also be closed between 6.30am and 5pm each day.

Special event clearway parking restrictions will be in effect on Hawkesbury Valley Way and Hobart St surrounding the airbase from 7am to 5pm each day.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

NRL Women's Preliminary Final: Sydney Roosters v Cronulla Sharks at polytec Stadium. Kick-off at 7.40pm, full-time around 9.20pm.

Traffic will be heavier than usual on roads approaching the stadium as fans travel to and from the stadium. Allow extra travel time and use local parking. 

Dane Drive will be closed before the match from 5.45pm between the Central Coast Highway and Donnison Street and will reopen once crowds have cleared the area.

NBL Illawarra Hawks v Tasmania Jackjumpers at WIN Entertainment Centre. Match starts at 8pm and finishes at 10pm.

Traffic may be heavier than usual on roads approaching the Wollongong CBD and on local roads around WIN Entertainment Centre as fans travel to the match.

Local roads around the stadium may close before, during and after the game for the safety of pedestrians.

Fans driving to the game on the freeway are encouraged to use the Masters Rd exit to avoid congestion at Mount Ousley Rd, both in and out of Wollongong.

Motorists should allow extra time for parking and be aware of increased pedestrian activity on local roads.
